description:
Make `jit validate <id>` and `jit validate <id> --explain` capture the repository once, compute the one report from the records the capture parsed, and call `ValidationReport::select` and `explain` on it directly, deleting `run_rules` and `explain_rules`.

## Background

- `run_rules` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:1643-1758`) and `explain_rules` (`:1993-2081`) read through storage and the executor's disk caches, evaluate graph rules over every issue, call the executor-side dangling-link and drift passes, and capture a whole validation image only to read plan documents (`image_plan_content`, `:1614-1623`). On a copy of this repository (1,863 issue files, release build) `jit validate <id>` takes 5.81 s against 4.53 s for whole-repository `jit validate`, even though whole validation also reads the event log and every gate run for record fidelity.
- Today's per-issue filter keeps every configuration error of a rule whose selector matches the issue, whoever fired it (`:1716-1720`), and folds in drift only when the rule set is unloadable (`:1656-1677`); explain keeps every configuration error (`:2025`).
- `run_rules(None)` (`:1724-1754`) is a second whole-repository report. Its only production caller passes `Some` (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:6006`, inside `if id.is_some()`); its test callers are `commands/batch_create.rs:1069`, `commands/validate.rs:3284`, `commands/gate_check.rs:2979,3415`, `tests/fast_docs_templates/batch_export_tests.rs:455` and `tests/fast_rules/validate_rule_runner_tests.rs:110`.
- The validation capture returns a `CapturedValidation` with the records it parsed. Whole-repository validation also derives the divergence view and the claims-index input and, as a history reader, the record-fidelity and document-reference verdicts; the issue selection excludes the structural failure.
- Other callers: `main.rs:5940` (explain), `tests/fast_rules/validate_rule_runner_tests.rs` and `tests/fast_rules/default_rules_registry_derivation_tests.rs:145`.
- Tests that re-prove filtering: `commands/validate.rs:3263`; `tests/fast_rules/validate_rule_runner_tests.rs:97,117,152`; `tests/cli_item_validate/validate_cli_rule_tests.rs:611,631`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit validate <id>` and `--explain` call `ValidationReport::select(&Selection::Issue(..))` and `ValidationReport::explain` directly on the report computed from one validation capture whose parsed records the report reads; no per-view wrapper remains (`run_rules` and `explain_rules` are deleted), and neither path reads storage, the executor's caches, a second capture, the event-log history or the gate-run listing. The whole-repository arm no longer exists, and its test callers read the whole report from the validation capture.
- [hard] REQ-02: The per-issue and explain paths derive no divergence view, no history verdict and no claims-index input, so their work is a subset of whole-repository validation's.
- [hard] REQ-03: Harness tests show that `jit validate <id>` omits a `container-from-label` pointer error fired by another issue under a rule matching the selected issue, and that with an unloadable rule set and an invariant bound to a rule it reports `rules-file` and no `enforcement-drift`; each fails on today's code, whose per-issue filter keeps the pointer error and reports drift.
- [hard] REQ-04: The listed filtering tests are reduced to wiring (the view equals the report's selection) or removed where the selection tests own the property; the CLI output and exit-code tests pass unchanged.

## Decisions

- **D-01** — Steward ruling 2026-11-04: the CLI and the checkers call the one `ValidationReport::select(&Selection)` entry point (and `ValidationReport::explain`) directly, with no per-view wrapper function; the issue, rule and scope views share one executor function that captures once and computes the report without history, which 2c8c13b2 introduces and 86f7e6eb and 208edf4c reuse. Rejected: per-view wrappers (`run_rules`, `explain_rules`, `validate_scope`, `validate_rule`), four thin copies around one selection.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: per-issue and explain configuration errors narrow to the selected issue's subject or rule; `rules-file` is always included and `enforcement-drift` never.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Per-issue and explain validation select from the report
